summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, calciphylaxis, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for altered mental status one day after discharge. He was found to have toxic metabolic encephalopathy likely due to opioid toxicity, as his confusion resolved after reducing his OxyContin and oxycodone doses. Workup showed no infection or acute intracranial process. His chronic left leg wound from recent necrotizing fasciitis debridement remained stable without infection, and dry gangrene in the fingers was non-progressive. Hypertension was managed with multiple agents, including increasing the clonidine patch. Kidney function improved slightly, with discharge creatinine of 2.5, and transplant medications were continued without rejection. He was discharged home with adjusted pain medications, wound care instructions, and close outpatient follow-up.
